content_html:
A refurbished iPad can be one of the better-value ways to buy an Apple tablet, especially if you do not need the newest model. The difficulty is that eBay has everything from low-cost older iPads to recent M-series models, and the cheapest listing is not always the best buy.

This guide focuses on five iPads that still make sense for US buyers in 2026. We have prioritized useful performance, sensible features and long-term usability rather than simply choosing the lowest advertised price.

Quick answer: which refurbished iPad should you buy?

  • Best overall value: iPad Air 5th generation.
  • Best for families and everyday use: iPad 10th generation.
  • Best for power users: 11-inch iPad Pro 3rd generation (M1).
  • Best compact choice: iPad mini 6th generation.
  • Best budget choice: iPad 9th generation.

1. iPad Air 5th generation — best overall refurbished iPad

The fifth-generation iPad Air is the model we would check first for most buyers. Its Apple M1 chip gives it far more performance headroom than many older standard iPads, while the 10.9-inch design is light enough to work well as a sofa tablet, travel device, student machine or lightweight laptop replacement with a keyboard.

It also uses USB-C and supports the second-generation Apple Pencil. The main compromise is storage: the base model has 64GB, which can feel tight if you keep lots of games, downloaded video or large creative files on the device.

Who should buy it: buyers who want the strongest balance of performance, portability and price without paying iPad Pro money.

What to check: storage capacity, whether a charger is included, screen condition and whether you genuinely need cellular. A higher-capacity Wi-Fi model can be more useful long term than a lower-capacity cellular model for many buyers.

2. iPad 10th generation — best for families and general use

The 10th-generation iPad is a strong mainstream choice if you mainly want web browsing, streaming, video calls, schoolwork, shopping, email and casual gaming. It moved the standard iPad to a more modern 10.9-inch design with USB-C, making it easier to share chargers and accessories with many newer devices.

Its performance is not as strong as the M1 iPad Air, but that does not matter much for everyday tablet use. A well-priced 10th-generation iPad can be the more sensible choice for a family device because you are not paying for performance you may never use.

Who should buy it: households, students and casual users who want a modern-looking iPad at a lower cost than an Air or Pro.

What to check: Wi-Fi versus cellular, storage capacity and accessory compatibility. Apple Pencil support is a little less straightforward on this model than on the Air 5, so check which Pencil you intend to use before buying accessories separately.

Compare current refurbished iPad 10th generation listings on eBay

3. 11-inch iPad Pro 3rd generation (M1) — best premium value

The 2021 11-inch iPad Pro is older on paper, but its M1 chip still gives it serious performance. It is the model to consider if you want a smoother 120Hz ProMotion display, stronger speakers, more capable cameras, Face ID and the flexibility of Apple's Pro accessories without buying a current-generation Pro at full retail pricing.

This is also the most interesting option for heavier multitasking, photo editing, illustration, music work or people who plan to connect the iPad to external displays and accessories. Refurbished Pro pricing can vary widely, so compare like-for-like storage, connectivity and condition.

Who should buy it: buyers who will actually use the better display, higher performance or premium hardware.

What to check: battery condition, screen uniformity, storage, included charger and cellular status. Read the full item specifics before buying.

Compare current refurbished 11-inch M1 iPad Pro listings on eBay

4. iPad mini 6th generation — best small iPad

The iPad mini 6 remains one of Apple's most distinctive tablets. Its 8.3-inch display makes it much easier to hold one-handed than a standard iPad, while the A15 Bionic chip provides capable performance for reading, travel, note-taking, games and media.

It also has USB-C and works particularly well for people who want a digital notebook or compact travel companion. The smaller screen is the whole point, but it is also the reason not to buy one: if you expect to spend hours using spreadsheets, split-screen apps or a keyboard case, a larger iPad is usually more comfortable.

Who should buy it: travelers, readers, commuters, note-takers and anyone who values portability above screen size.

What to check: storage, Wi-Fi versus cellular and the screen edges for impact damage. Because mini models can retain value well, compare the price with larger refurbished iPads before assuming the smaller tablet is automatically cheaper.

5. iPad 9th generation — best budget refurbished iPad

If the goal is to spend as little as possible while still getting a capable iPad, the 9th-generation model deserves a look. It uses the older design with a Home button and Lightning connector, but it remains practical for streaming, browsing, children's apps, FaceTime, school portals and basic productivity.

The biggest reason to choose it is value. It can make particular sense as a first tablet, a shared family device or a secondary screen for around the house when the saving versus newer models is substantial.

Who should buy it: budget-conscious buyers who care more about function than having the latest design.

What to check: storage, battery condition and whether you are happy to keep using Lightning accessories. If the price gets too close to a refurbished 10th-generation iPad, we would usually move up to the newer design instead.

Compare current refurbished iPad 9th generation listings on eBay

How much should you spend on a refurbished iPad?

There is no single correct price because eBay listings change constantly and the same iPad can be offered in several storage capacities, cosmetic grades and connectivity versions. A useful way to shop is to decide which model you want first, then compare several listings with the same storage and Wi-Fi or cellular specification.

Do not compare a lower-capacity Good-condition Wi-Fi model directly with a higher-capacity Excellent-condition cellular model. The headline price difference may be justified. Also check shipping costs and return terms, because a slightly more expensive listing can still be the better overall deal.

What should you look for in an eBay refurbished listing?

Read the individual listing carefully rather than relying on the word "refurbished" alone. Look for a clear condition description, seller feedback, testing information, included accessories, warranty terms and the return policy. Those details can matter more than a small saving on the purchase price.

Seven checks before buying a refurbished iPad on eBay

  1. Check the exact generation. iPad names are repetitive, so verify the generation, model year and screen size.
  2. Compare the same storage capacity. A higher-capacity model should not be compared directly with a base-storage model.
  3. Confirm Wi-Fi or cellular. Cellular models may cost more, and carrier or unlocked status matters if you plan to add a data plan.
  4. Read the cosmetic description. A lower grade can be good value if you are happy with visible wear.
  5. Check seller feedback and sales history. A high-volume seller with strong recent feedback can be worth prioritizing over the absolute cheapest listing.
  6. Read the returns and warranty terms. These matter more on refurbished electronics than a small difference in purchase price.
  7. Check what is included. Do not assume an Apple charger, cable, Pencil or keyboard is included unless the listing says so.

Which refurbished iPad would we buy?

For most people, the iPad Air 5th generation is our first choice because the M1 chip, USB-C design and strong accessory support give it an unusually good balance of longevity and price. If you simply want an iPad for family use, streaming and everyday tasks, the 10th-generation iPad can be the smarter purchase when it is meaningfully cheaper.

At the low end, the 9th-generation iPad remains compelling when the saving is substantial. At the high end, the M1 11-inch iPad Pro is the model to watch if you want premium hardware and can find the right configuration at a sensible refurbished price. The iPad mini 6 is less about bargain hunting and more about buying the compact form factor because you specifically want it.

Guide updated September 15, 2026. Prices, availability, seller terms and condition grades change frequently. Always check the live eBay listing before purchasing.
